pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Louisiana does not use one single statewide journeyman electrician exam for every candidate. Journeyman electrician licensing, registration, and testing requirements are commonly set by local jurisdictions. A candidate may need to follow the rules of a city, parish, municipal licensing board, contractor licensing department, local building department, or other local authority. A commonly used journeyman-level electrical exam format is the ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam. That exam includes 80 multiple-choice questions, allows 4 hours of testing time, and is open book. Its subject areas include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam places strong emphasis on wiring methods and materials, branch circuits and conductors, equipment and devices, services and service equipment, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions. These are practical journeyman-level areas that require candidates to understand both NEC rules and field application. Some Louisiana cities or parishes may use different approved exams, local applications, separate passing scores, local code amendments, different testing providers, or specific experience documentation. Candidates preparing for a Louisiana journeyman electrician credential should match their study materials to the exam required by the jurisdiction where they are applying. This Ultimate Combo is focused on 2026 NEC-based journeyman electrician exam preparation. pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates taking that exam may use approved reference materials during the examination, subject to the exam provider’s rules. Because Louisiana journeyman electrician testing is commonly controlled at the local level, candidates must follow the exam-room rules for the specific exam they are scheduled to take. Open book testing still requires strong preparation. The National Electrical Code is a detailed technical reference, and a candidate who is unfamiliar with its structure can lose valuable time searching through unrelated articles. A prepared candidate should be able to identify the subject of the question, locate the correct NEC article or table, interpret the wording, and apply the rule accurately. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Louisiana journeyman electrician licensing steps depend on the local authority that issues or recognizes the credential. A candidate may need to apply through a city licensing office, parish department, municipal board, local building department, or electrical licensing authority. Since Louisiana does not issue one uniform statewide journeyman electrician license, identifying the correct local jurisdiction is the first step. A typical Louisiana journeyman electrician path may include completing supervised electrical work experience, finishing apprenticeship or classroom training when required, gathering employer verification, submitting a local application, paying required local fees, scheduling the approved electrical examination, passing the required exam, and completing any remaining local licensing or registration steps.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Local requirements may include a minimum number of years or hours of electrical experience, proof of work under a licensed electrician or electrical contractor, apprenticeship completion, classroom instruction, identification documents, continuing education, or a local sponsor. Some jurisdictions may recognize an exam passed through a national provider, while others may require a specific local exam or local review process. Louisiana electrical contractor licensing is separate from local journeyman-level credentialing. Electrical contracting at the state level is regulated through the Louisiana State Licensing Board for Contractors when the work falls within the contractor licensing threshold and classification requirements. A journeyman credential generally supports trade-level work and employment, while contracting authority requires the proper contractor licensing, business structure, and regulatory approval.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Louisiana journeyman electrician requirements are commonly handled locally. Cities, parishes, and municipalities may set their own rules for journeyman electricians, master electricians, electrical contractors, permits, registrations, renewals, and local work authorization. Because of this local structure, candidates should prepare for the rules of the jurisdiction where the credential is needed. One local authority may require a journeyman electrician exam and documented field experience, while another may recognize a national journeyman-level exam or focus on contractor registration. Some employers may also require a journeyman-level credential as part of hiring, promotion, or jobsite qualification standards. Common preparation areas for Louisiana journeyman electrician candidates include National Electrical Code knowledge, electrical theory, services, feeders, branch circuits, conductors, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, motors, control devices, equipment, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and electrical calculations.
